title: The Campus, the Exchange, and the Twenty-Five Years: Stanford to Lompoc
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Stanford, born to two law professors
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: In the hospital on the university's own campus a son is born to Joseph Bankman and Barbara Fried, both professors at Stanford Law School. The father teaches tax; the mother writes on distributive justice, on what people owe one another and how the debt might be counted. The house he is brought home to argues for sport, and the argument has a method: expected value, consequences totted up, the good treated as a quantity that can in principle be measured and then maximised. A second son, Gabriel, arrives three years later.
suggested_refs: Stanford Law School faculty rosters of the 1990s, listing both parents

stops.name: Stanford campus, a childhood inside the university
stops.date_confidence: inferred. The childhood on campus in faculty housing is attested by Michael Lewis, Going Infinite (2023), without a precise date; dated here to order the segment. Note that the chronology lens places the parents' house in Palo Alto and the geography lens in Stanford; Wikipedia's 'Joseph Bankman' says Stanford, and this file follows it. Not adjudicated further.
stops.campa: He grows up on the campus itself, in faculty housing, among neighbours who all teach and children who are all the children of people who teach. At thirty he will be brought back to this address wearing a location monitor and confined to it for eight months. For now the utilitarian calculus is the household language, spoken at dinner the way other families discuss the weather. He plays games with rules and is quick at anything that can be scored, and the world past the campus edge exists mostly as a set of numbers that could be improved.
suggested_refs: Michael Lewis, Going Infinite (2023), on the Stanford childhood

stops.name: Hillsborough, Crystal Springs Uplands School
stops.date_confidence: attendance attested (Wikipedia); the enrolment year is inferred backward from his 2010 matriculation at MIT. Mathcamp attendance is attested but the year and host campus are recorded nowhere reachable, since the programme rotates its host college annually.
stops.campa: Twenty miles north of home, at a small private school in Hillsborough above the reservoir, he takes the standard route of the mathematically quick: contests, proofs, an aptitude that outruns the syllabus. He applies east. In these years he also attends Canada/USA Mathcamp, the summer programme that gathers such teenagers out of two countries and turns them loose on graduate material for five weeks. Which summer, and on which campus, nobody has recorded; the programme moves its host college every year.
suggested_refs: Canada/USA Mathcamp alumni rosters, which do not name his year
sources: New York Times, 'Sam Bankman-Fried Tries to Explain Himself' (2022)

segments.name: Cambridge, and the Argument for Getting Rich

stops.name: Cambridge, matriculation at MIT
stops.date_confidence: attested for the degree and the field; the September 2010 matriculation is inferred from a 2014 graduation.
stops.campa: He enters MIT to read physics, with a minor in mathematics. The department turns out theorists and, in far greater numbers, graduates hired by trading firms for their fluency with probability and their tolerance for being wrong in public. He is quick, restless, and unimpressed by the physics itself. Gary Wang, who will build an exchange with him six years later, is in the same undergraduate years. Nobody here treats a physics degree used for nothing as a loss; it is the ordinary outcome. He takes his in 2014.
suggested_refs: MIT Department of Physics degree records, class of 2014

stops.name: Brookline, the house at 259 St. Paul Street
stops.date_confidence: residence attested (Wikipedia); the year within his undergraduate span is not specified and is set here to order the segment. Coordinates from OpenStreetMap. Note that the gathering pass placed Epsilon Theta in Cambridge near Kendall Square, 2.7 km away and in the wrong municipality; corrected.
stops.campa: He lives not on campus but two and a half miles west, in Brookline, at Epsilon Theta, 259 St. Paul Street, an independent living group of the kind MIT keeps at arm's length: a shared house, coeducational, self-governing, some thirty residents cooking and arguing and running their own affairs. The house is a small society of precisely the sort of people he will later hire, and he will not afterwards distinguish a household from a firm. The commute to campus is a subway ride.
suggested_refs: Epsilon Theta, 259 St. Paul Street, Brookline, an MIT Independent Living Group

stops.name: Cambridge, lunch with William MacAskill
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The scene appears in neither Wikipedia's 'Sam Bankman-Fried' nor its 'William MacAskill'; it descends through the Sequoia, New Yorker and Michael Lewis retellings, and the year 2012 is not independently anchored anywhere reachable. The citation to 'Wikipedia, Effective Altruism' attached to it in the research pool was false and has been struck.
stops.campa: A young Oxford philosopher comes to MIT and sits down to lunch with an undergraduate who does not know what to do with himself. He will repeat the argument for ten years, almost word for word. It is compact: a doctor saves some number of lives with his own hands, but a banker who gives away most of a large salary funds many doctors, so the ethical career may be the lucrative one. Earning to give. The undergraduate was raised on exactly this arithmetic and takes it as a permission slip and a job description at once. Nobody who retells the scene afterwards can say what year it happened in.
suggested_refs: William MacAskill, Doing Good Better (2015), for the earning-to-give argument in its author's own words
sources: Journalistic retellings: Sequoia Capital profile (2022), New Yorker profile of MacAskill (2022), Michael Lewis, Going Infinite (2023)

segments.name: The Desk, and the Japan Premium

stops.name: Lower Manhattan, the summer at Jane Street
stops.date_confidence: the 2013 internship is attested; the month is conventional for a summer programme. The building is not: the research pool pinned this at 250 Vesey Street, which is Jane Street's present headquarters, with no move date recorded anywhere reachable, and the firm occupied One New York Plaza earlier in the decade. The stop is therefore neighbourhood-level and carries no street number.
stops.campa: He interns at Jane Street Capital, a proprietary trading firm that hires mathematicians and teaches them to price risk in fractions of a second. The training is famously done through games: bets on trivia, on coin flips, on anything with a distribution, played until estimating an edge under uncertainty becomes reflex. The culture rewards being approximately right at speed and punishes nothing so much as certainty. He is good at it immediately, and is asked back.
suggested_refs: Jane Street's internship recruitment materials of the early 2010s, built around probability games

stops.name: Lower Manhattan, three years on the exchange-traded funds desk
stops.date_confidence: the 2014 start and the September 2017 departure are attested; the specific desk is reported rather than documented in the sources reachable here. Same address caveat as the preceding stop.
stops.campa: Out of MIT he returns to Jane Street full time and trades international exchange-traded funds: arbitrage across borders and time zones, the business of noticing that the same thing carries two different prices in two different places and standing in the gap between them. He gives away a portion of his salary as the philosophy prescribes and tells colleagues he means to give away far more. He leaves in September 2017. Three years on that desk is the whole of his formal training in finance.
suggested_refs: Jane Street Capital's international ETF business, the trade he carried into crypto

stops.name: Berkeley, the Centre for Effective Altruism
stops.date_confidence: attested, October to November 2017. The research pool rendered this date '1917-10', a century-off typo, one of four in the same pool; corrected.
stops.campa: He quits the desk, moves to Berkeley, and takes a post as director of development at the American office of the movement that gave him his career logic, the Centre for Effective Altruism. October to November: it lasts weeks. Fundraising for a philosophy is slower than trading and pays nothing, and the arbitrage instinct is already looking elsewhere, at a market of retail speculators and unregulated venues where the price gaps are of a size no equity desk in New York has seen in decades.
suggested_refs: Centre for Effective Altruism staff records, October to November 2017

stops.name: Berkeley, Alameda Research founded
stops.date_confidence: founding month contested and not resolved: Wikipedia's 'Alameda Research' says September 2017, Wikipedia's 'Sam Bankman-Fried' says November 2017, the same encyclopedia disagreeing with itself. Dated November here to order the segment after the Centre for Effective Altruism post. The research pool's '1917-11' is a century-off typo, corrected. The pool also named Caroline Ellison a co-founder; she was not, and joined in 2018.
stops.campa: With Tara Mac Aulay he founds a quantitative trading firm and gives it a name chosen for its blandness, so that a bank reading the wire transfers will see a California county and not a crypto fund. Almost nobody involved is thirty. The staff come out of the effective altruism community and out of Jane Street, willing to work in a house they also sleep in, paid partly in the understanding that the profits are going to charity. Caroline Ellison joins the following year. The founding month is not agreed; the same encyclopedia says September in one article and November in another.
suggested_refs: The name Alameda Research, chosen to pass unremarked in banking correspondence

stops.name: Tokyo, the Japan premium
stops.date_confidence: attested for January 2018 and for the scale of the trade; the Tokyo pin is central and unaddressed, since no source names the branch or the office. The research pool dated this '1918-01', corrected, and called it a kimchi-premium trade, which names the Korean spread rather than the Japanese one.
stops.campa: Bitcoin trades higher in Japan than in the United States and the gap will not close, because the capital cannot move fast enough to close it. He flies to Tokyo because Japanese banks require a body in the branch to open an account, and once the account is open Alameda moves as much as twenty-five million dollars a day across the spread. He has read almost nothing about the asset he is arbitraging. It was bootstrapped nine years earlier by Hal Finney, who ran the second node on the network and took the first transaction ever sent.
stops.quote: I got involved in crypto without any idea what crypto was... It just seemed like there was a lot of good trading to do.
stops.quote_source: Steven Ehrlich, 'Meet The World's Richest 29-Year-Old', Forbes, 6 October 2021, as reproduced in Wikiquote's raw wikitext; the Forbes original returns HTTP 403 from this environment
suggested_refs: The Japan-United States bitcoin spread of January 2018, and the bank account opened in person to work it
sources: hal_finney.journey.json, for the first transaction of January 2009

segments.name: Hong Kong, the Exchange Built for Its Own House

stops.name: Macau, the conference
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. Wikipedia names Macau as the location of the conference and links the trip to the Hong Kong move, but gives no venue and no month; the date orders the segment only. Coordinates are a peninsula placeholder. The research pool's coordinates were in Cotai, 5 km from the district its own note claimed.
stops.campa: He crosses to Macau for a cryptocurrency conference, one of a circuit of events where the industry sells itself to itself in casino ballrooms. The ferry from Hong Kong takes an hour. What he finds is that the entire trading world of the asset he now depends on runs out of Asia, on Asian hours, under regulators who have not yet decided what any of it is. Within months the firm and everyone in it will have moved to Hong Kong. He does not go back to California.
suggested_refs: The Macau cryptocurrency conference circuit of 2018, venue unrecorded

stops.name: Central, Hong Kong, Alameda moves east
stops.date_confidence: attested for early 2019. No specific office building or address is confirmed in any reachable source, so the pin is district-level. The research pool rendered this '1919-01', corrected.
stops.campa: In early 2019 the firm moves its headquarters from California to Hong Kong, a jurisdiction with no capital gains tax, no restriction on crypto derivatives, and no regulator yet claiming the industry as its own. Alameda trades around the clock. The staff live together again, as they did in Berkeley and as they will in Nassau, so that the trading firm and the household are the same people in the same rooms. The address of the office appears in no reporting at all.
suggested_refs: Hong Kong's derivatives regime of 2019, under which the exchange was built

stops.name: Hong Kong, FTX incorporated
stops.date_confidence: attested: founded April 2019, opened May 2019. The research pool collapsed the two into one May date and rendered the year as 1919; both corrected.
stops.campa: He incorporates an exchange of his own in April, with Gary Wang, a friend from MIT who has come out of Google's engineering ranks. The stated reason is that the existing venues are badly built: they liquidate positions clumsily, they socialise losses across all users, they cannot handle a serious trader. The unstated structure is simpler. The exchange's largest customer will be Alameda Research, which he owns roughly ninety percent of. None of this is concealed in 2019. It is in the filings.
suggested_refs: FTX's founding documents, April 2019, and the Alameda ownership stake reported in the Forbes 400 of that year

stops.name: Hong Kong, the exchange opens for trading
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: The exchange opens in May with futures, leveraged tokens and an index product, and grows faster than anyone has forecast. Volume follows liquidity and liquidity follows Alameda, which stands ready to take the other side of nearly anything, so the order book is never thin and the venue never looks empty. Within two years FTX will be clearing billions of dollars a day. Binance takes an early equity stake in the first year, and will hold it until he buys it back in July 2021.
suggested_refs: FTX's leveraged tokens and index futures, the products it opened with

stops.name: Hong Kong, the Blockfolio purchase
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: FTX pays about one hundred and fifty million dollars for Blockfolio, a portfolio-tracking app with several million retail users and no exchange of its own. The logic is distribution: the app is where ordinary people already look at their coins, and the exchange wants to be the button they press next. It is his first large acquisition. Bigger ones follow, on the same reasoning: buy attention wherever attention has already pooled, at whatever price is asked.
suggested_refs: Blockfolio's retail user base, acquired August 2020 and folded into FTX

stops.name: Hong Kong, the eighteen billion dollar round
stops.date_confidence: attested for the Series B valuation and the Binance buyout; the Forbes 400 placement and the 30 Under 30 listing are attested to the year 2021 without a month.
stops.campa: A Series B values the exchange at eighteen billion dollars, and he uses part of the proceeds to buy out Binance's early stake, a separation that costs him and that he judges worth the cost. Forbes will rank him the forty-first richest American this year, the fortune resting almost entirely on his ownership of Alameda Research, and will put him on its list of the notable young. He is twenty-nine. The buyout leaves Changpeng Zhao holding a large position in FTT, the exchange's own token, in place of equity.
suggested_refs: The FTT token taken by Binance in lieu of equity, July 2021

stops.name: Albany, New Providence, the move to the Bahamas
stops.date_confidence: attested for September 2021. Coordinates from OpenStreetMap; the research pool carried two different and both incorrect sets of coordinates for Albany, 3.5 km and 3.3 km out respectively, and this file standardises on the resort's actual position.
stops.campa: The exchange moves its headquarters from Hong Kong to Nassau, and the staff move with it into Albany, a gated resort on the south shore of New Providence with a marina built for very large boats. Nothing about the move is hidden; it is announced and photographed. The country's securities regulator is a short drive away and has a fraction of the staff of the American agencies that will eventually take the company apart. The commute to the office is a golf cart.
suggested_refs: The Albany resort, Adelaide Road, New Providence, and the Securities Commission of the Bahamas

stops.name: Albany, the penthouse
stops.date_confidence: attested for the arrangement (Forbes, 2022); the month is set to order the segment, since the reporting gives 2021 to 2022 as a span. The quotation is from a Sequoia Capital profile of September 2022, later removed from Sequoia's site and reachable here only through Wikiquote.
stops.campa: He lives in a five-bedroom penthouse in the Albany complex with about ten colleagues from Alameda and FTX. Several of them are or have been in relationships with each other and with him, Caroline Ellison among them, who becomes co-chief executive of Alameda and then, in August 2022, its sole chief executive. Forbes reports all of this while the exchange is still growing, and it is read as eccentricity. There is no line anywhere between the firm, the fund and the house. He says he does not read books.
stops.quote: I would never read a book... I'm very skeptical of books.
stops.quote_source: Sequoia Capital profile, 22 September 2022, as reproduced in Wikiquote; the original page has been removed and the archive fetch was blocked
suggested_refs: Forbes, 'Inside the Bizarre Sex-Fueled Dynamics of FTX' (2022)

stops.name: Washington, testimony before the House
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: He appears before the House Committee on Financial Services in the Rayburn building as the presentable face of an industry that badly needs one: young, rich, visibly indifferent to how he looks, and asking to be regulated. He is by this point among the largest individual donors in American politics. He proposes a framework in which his own exchange's risk engine would serve as the model. Members thank him for coming. The date is the eighth of December, 2021.
suggested_refs: C-SPAN recording of the House Financial Services Committee hearing, 8 December 2021

stops.name: Nassau, the thirty-two billion dollar valuation
stops.date_confidence: attested for the Series C and the venture fund, both January 2022. The arena and advertising material folded into this campa carries its own dates: the naming rights were announced March 2021, took effect June 2021 after league approval, and were terminated January 2023 in the bankruptcy; the Super Bowl LVI advertisement aired 13 February 2022. His own presence at either the arena or the stadium is nowhere attested, which is why neither has a stop.
stops.campa: A Series C prices the exchange at thirty-two billion dollars, and in the same month FTX announces a venture fund of two billion to buy whatever the industry produces next. The money is not being spent to sell a product; it is being spent to look permanent. The naming rights to the Miami Heat's arena are already his, nineteen years for a hundred and thirty-five million dollars, signed the previous June. A Super Bowl advertisement starring Larry David is six weeks away.
suggested_refs: The FTX Arena naming-rights agreement, June 2021 to January 2023
The Larry David advertisement for FTX, Super Bowl LVI, 13 February 2022
sources: Ad Age coverage of the Super Bowl LVI advertisement

stops.name: Baha Mar, the Crypto Bahamas conference
stops.date_confidence: attested to April 2022; the exact day within the conference is set for ordering. Coordinates corrected from the research pool, which was 4.9 km west of the resort.
stops.campa: At the Baha Mar resort on Cable Beach he hosts a conference of his own, with Bill Clinton and Tony Blair together on the stage and Katy Perry in the room, an assembly of former heads of government and pop stars convened by a man of thirty to discuss the future of money. He moderates. Seven months later the company is in Chapter 11. The photographs from that week will circulate for years afterwards as evidence of something, though of what exactly is still argued.
suggested_refs: The Crypto Bahamas conference, Baha Mar, Cable Beach, April 2022
sources: Reuters and Bloomberg coverage of Crypto Bahamas 2022

stops.name: Albany, the Giving Pledge and the Future Fund
stops.date_confidence: the Giving Pledge signature is attested to June 2022; the Future Fund's commitment total is attested as of September 2022 and is folded into the same stop.
stops.campa: He signs the Giving Pledge, committing in public to give away the majority of his fortune. By September the Future Fund he has endowed has committed roughly one hundred and sixty million dollars to about a hundred and ten organisations working on pandemics, on artificial intelligence risk, on the long-term future of a species he speaks of in the plural. Nobody funded by it asks in the summer of 2022 where the money came from. The grants are real and the money arrives in the accounts.
suggested_refs: The FTX Future Fund grant list as it stood in September 2022
sources: Future Fund team resignation letter, EA Forum, 10 November 2022

stops.name: Nassau, the balance sheet in print
stops.date_confidence: attested for the CoinDesk publication date; the Nassau pin is where he was, not where the article was written.
stops.campa: CoinDesk publishes a leaked balance sheet for Alameda Research. Of roughly fourteen and a half billion dollars in assets, some three and a half billion is FTT, the token issued by the exchange he also owns, most of it unlocked and none of it saleable at anything resembling the quoted price. The fund's collateral is paper printed by the exchange the fund trades on. The story runs on a Wednesday. For four days almost nothing happens, and he goes on posting as usual.
suggested_refs: The leaked Alameda Research balance sheet published by CoinDesk, 2 November 2022

stops.name: Nassau, Zhao sells
stops.date_confidence: attested. The research pool dated this 8 November, two days late; the distinction matters, because 6 November is the trigger of the run and 8 November is the letter of intent, a separate event.
stops.campa: It takes a single post. On the sixth of November the chief executive of Binance announces that his company will liquidate its entire FTT position, the token it accepted in place of equity when it was bought out sixteen months earlier. He frames it as ordinary risk management. Everyone reads it as a declaration. Withdrawal requests arrive at FTX faster than they can be filled: six billion dollars in seventy-two hours. The money that would have filled them is in Alameda Research, where it was moved.
suggested_refs: Changpeng Zhao's announcement of Binance's FTT liquidation, 6 November 2022

stops.name: Nassau, FTX is fine
stops.date_confidence: attested. The original post has since been deleted and X blocked direct retrieval from this environment, so the wording is taken from Wikipedia's reproduction.
stops.campa: He posts that the exchange is fine and its assets are fine, that FTX holds enough to cover client holdings, that withdrawals are processing normally. On the same day FTT loses roughly eighty percent of its value and Binance signs a non-binding letter of intent to buy the company outright, an announcement that reads as a rescue for about twenty-four hours. Withdrawals halt the following morning. The next day Binance withdraws, citing mishandled customer funds and reports of federal investigations.
stops.quote: FTX is fine. Assets are fine.
stops.quote_source: Post by @SBF_FTX, 8 November 2022, deleted; text as quoted in Wikipedia, 'Sam Bankman-Fried'
suggested_refs: The deleted @SBF_FTX post of 8 November 2022, preserved only in secondary quotation

stops.name: Nassau, Chapter 11
stops.date_confidence: attested. The filing itself was made in Delaware; the stop is pinned where he was.
stops.campa: On the eleventh of November FTX, Alameda Research and more than a hundred and thirty affiliated companies file for bankruptcy protection in Delaware, and he resigns as chief executive. The entire staff of the Future Fund had resigned the day before, saying they could not reconcile what they had been told with what was now alleged. He stays in the Bahamas and answers everyone who calls. John J. Ray III, the restructuring lawyer who wound up Enron, takes the company over.
suggested_refs: The Chapter 11 petition of FTX Trading Ltd. and affiliates, District of Delaware, 11 November 2022
sources: Future Fund team resignation letter, EA Forum

stops.name: Albany, the messages to Kelsey Piper
stops.date_confidence: attested for the publication date. Vox blocked direct retrieval from this environment; the wording is taken from Wikipedia's reproduction of the exchange, and the quoted fragment is a fragment, not a whole sentence in the original.
stops.campa: Five days after the bankruptcy he answers a Vox reporter's direct messages for hours, apparently without weighing that they might be published. He says the talk of regulation was public relations, that the regulators he courted make everything worse and do not protect customers at all, that the ethics was mostly a front. Asked about the good he had promised to do, he calls the whole vocabulary a game played by people like him so that everyone will like them. It runs the same day.
stops.quote: dumb game we woke Westerners play where we say all the right shibboleths and so everyone likes us
stops.quote_source: Direct messages to Kelsey Piper, Vox, published 16 November 2022, as reproduced in Wikipedia, 'Sam Bankman-Fried'
suggested_refs: Kelsey Piper, 'Sam Bankman-Fried tries to explain himself', Vox, 16 November 2022

stops.name: Albany, arrested
stops.date_confidence: attested for the date and for the Bahamian arrest at United States request. The prepared testimony is quoted in the sources only in bracket-edited form, '[FTX] is solvent', in a Guardian live blog of 13 December 2022, so the claim is stated here in plain prose rather than quoted.
stops.campa: Bahamian police arrest him at the Albany complex at the request of United States prosecutors, on the night before he is due to testify by video to the House Committee on Financial Services. He had a text prepared for the committee, never delivered, maintaining that FTX was solvent and that the company's general counsel, Ryne Miller, had pressured him into declaring bankruptcy. The Southern District of New York unseals the indictment the next morning: wire fraud, securities fraud, commodities fraud, money laundering, conspiracy.
suggested_refs: The undelivered prepared testimony of 13 December 2022
Kari Paul's Guardian live blog of the hearing, 13 December 2022
sources: Kari Paul, The Guardian live blog, 13 December 2022

stops.name: Fox Hill, nine days in the Bahamian prison
stops.date_confidence: attested for roughly ten days of detention at Fox Hill in December 2022. Coordinates corrected from the research pool, which was 6.5 km out in the wrong part of eastern New Providence.
stops.campa: He is held at the Bahamas Department of Correctional Services at Fox Hill, a prison with a long and documented record of overcrowding, poor sanitation and violence, while he contests extradition. His lawyers ask that he be released to house arrest in Nassau. The magistrate refuses. He contests for nine days and then stops. The indictment waiting for him in New York, unsealed the morning after his arrest, runs to eight counts. His American counsel had advised exactly that on the first morning.
suggested_refs: United States State Department human rights reporting on conditions at Fox Hill
sources: Reuters coverage of the extradition proceedings

stops.name: Lynden Pindling International Airport, the flight north
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: He is driven from Fox Hill to the airport and put aboard a chartered aircraft with federal agents on either side of him, having waived his right to contest extradition in a Nassau courtroom that morning. Fifteen months earlier he had brought an entire company to this island, and the island had rewritten its financial law to keep companies like it. The flight to New York takes about three hours. He is thirty years old and has been in custody for nine days.
suggested_refs: The Bahamian extradition waiver of 21 December 2022
sources: Associated Press coverage of the extradition

stops.name: White Plains, into American custody
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: The aircraft lands at the small airport at White Plains, north of the city, which the government prefers to a commercial field for arrivals it would rather not stage. He is taken into custody by FBI agents on the tarmac and driven south into Manhattan. His parents have flown in from California. Photographers are waiting at the fence, and the pictures from the runway are the first of him in custody. It is the twenty-first of December, and he is due in federal court the next morning.
suggested_refs: Westchester County Airport, standard arrival point for extraditions into the Southern District
sources: Associated Press and Reuters coverage of the extradition

stops.name: Foley Square, the arraignment
stops.date_confidence: attested for the arraignment and the bond amount. That the bond was largely unsecured, resting on the parents' house and family signatures rather than cash, is widely reported and is not in the research pool as a primary citation.
stops.campa: He appears at the Daniel Patrick Moynihan United States Courthouse on Pearl Street, in a suit, before a magistrate. The government does not oppose bail. The package is two hundred and fifty million dollars, the largest pretrial bond in American criminal history. It is a number rather than a payment: secured by his parents' house and by signatures, almost none of it in cash. The figure runs as a headline for a week; the structure behind it is reported almost nowhere. He is released to his parents' custody.
suggested_refs: The bail package filed in United States v. Bankman-Fried, S.D.N.Y., 22 December 2022

stops.name: Stanford, eight months in his parents' house
stops.date_confidence: attested for the confinement, which ran from release after the 22 December 2022 arraignment to the bail revocation of 11 August 2023. The research pool's geography lens gave the correct span; its chronology lens dated the start to February 2023 and placed the house in Palo Alto, and both of those are wrong.
stops.campa: He returns to the faculty housing he grew up in, to a bedroom in his parents' house, with a location monitor on his ankle and a court order confining him to the property. He plays video games. He writes long documents and circulates them to journalists. He is thirty years old and cannot walk off a lawn he has known since he was a child. In February a judge tightens the terms after he contacts former FTX employees. The arrangement holds until August.
suggested_refs: The bail conditions of 22 December 2022 and their amendment of 1 February 2023
sources: New York Times coverage of the bail conditions

stops.name: Foley Square, not guilty
stops.date_confidence: attested for the plea. That Ellison and Wang had by then pleaded guilty and agreed to cooperate is reported outside the supplied research pool, which attests them as cooperating witnesses and gives their 2024 sentencings without the plea dates.
stops.campa: He pleads not guilty before Judge Lewis A. Kaplan, who will preside over everything that follows and who runs a courtroom with no appetite for theatre. Trial is set for October. Two of the people he lived and worked with in Nassau, Caroline Ellison and Gary Wang, have already agreed to cooperate with the government. The case against him will be made by the people who slept in the next rooms. He goes back to California within the week, to the ankle monitor and the childhood bedroom.
suggested_refs: United States v. Bankman-Fried, arraignment and plea, S.D.N.Y., 3 January 2023

stops.name: Foley Square, the superseding indictments
stops.date_confidence: attested for the February 2023 counts and for the March 2023 bribery count, folded into the same stop. The August 2023 figure of roughly one hundred million dollars of customer money routed into politics is a prosecutors' allegation and is carried as reconstruction. The quotation is from post-collapse recorded conversations with Tiffany Fong, reported by The Guardian, 30 November 2022, not from the February 2022 interview the research pool named.
stops.campa: Prosecutors add four counts, among them a scheme to make more than three hundred illegal political contributions in other people's names, so that money could appear on both sides of American politics without appearing under his. A month later a further count alleges he directed a forty million dollar bribe to Chinese officials to unfreeze Alameda accounts. By August the government puts the sum of misappropriated customer money routed into politics at roughly a hundred million dollars.
stops.quote: All my Republican donations were dark
stops.quote_source: Sam Bankman-Fried in recorded conversations with Tiffany Fong, reported by Dominic Rushe, The Guardian, 30 November 2022; he gave as his reason that the press were 'super liberal'
suggested_refs: The superseding indictments of February and March 2023
Dominic Rushe, 'FTX billionaire Sam Bankman-Fried funneled dark money to Republicans', The Guardian, 30 November 2022

stops.name: Sunset Park, the Metropolitan Detention Center
stops.date_confidence: attested. Coordinates corrected from the research pool, which was 1.1 km out and landed in Red Hook.
stops.campa: Judge Kaplan revokes bail, finding that he has tampered with witnesses, and remands him to the Metropolitan Detention Center in Sunset Park, Brooklyn: a federal jail with its own documented record of lockdowns, power failures and understaffing. It is the eleventh of August, eight months after the arraignment. He prepares for trial from there, reading discovery on a laptop in a shared room, on the jail's schedule rather than his own. Trial is seven weeks away.

stops.name: Foley Square, the trial opens
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: The trial begins on the third of October. The government's case runs on the testimony of the people who were closest to him: Ellison, Wang, Nishad Singh, each of whom has pleaded guilty, each of whom describes being directed to move customer money into Alameda. Michael Lewis publishes Going Infinite in the same week, from months of access inside the company before it collapsed, and it is in shop windows while the jury is being selected. The book finds him more interesting than culpable.

stops.name: Foley Square, guilty on all seven counts
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: The jury convicts him on all seven counts: two of wire fraud and five of conspiracy, covering securities fraud, commodities fraud and money laundering. The sums at issue are customers' deposits, money placed with an exchange for safekeeping and moved into a trading firm the same man owned. The verdict is returned on the second of November, a month and a day after the trial opened. He had taken the stand in his own defence, which most defendants do not. His parents are in the courtroom. He is thirty-one years old.

stops.name: Foley Square, the sentence
stops.date_confidence: attested for the sentence and the forfeiture amount; the effective term of roughly eighteen years is an estimate applying First Step Act credits, not a figure from the bench.
stops.campa: Judge Kaplan sentences him to twenty-five years in federal prison and orders the forfeiture of eleven billion and twenty million dollars. With credits under the First Step Act the effective term is reckoned at something near eighteen. His mother, a professor who has spent a career writing about responsibility and desert and who owes what to whom, had written to the judge in February asking for leniency. Federal sentences carry no parole. He is taken out through the side door of the courtroom.

Coordinates corrected from the research pool by about 540 metres. Note an unresolved conflict in the sources about custody in 2024: one lens reports an assignment to FCI Lompoc after sentencing, another reports Lompoc only after Terminal Island. Not adjudicated.
stops.campa: He is moved to a low-security federal institution on an island in Los Angeles harbour, register number 37244-510, within sight of the container cranes of the port. In March he gives an interview to Tucker Carlson from inside, without authorisation from the Bureau of Prisons, and speaks in terms that reporters read as an application for a presidential pardon. He is reported afterwards to have been placed in solitary confinement. An account in his name begins posting approval of the administration's policies on drugs, the economy and crypto.

stops.name: Lompoc, the appeal denied and the prison closed
stops.date_confidence: the appeal denial of 12 June 2026 is carried from a secondary summary; the primary Second Circuit docket was not reachable from this environment. The closure of FCI Terminal Island on 13 June 2026 and the transfer to FCI Lompoc I are attested by Wikipedia's articles on both institutions, the latter listing him among current inmates. Coordinates corrected from the research pool by about 4 km. This is the last verifiable stop as of August 2026; he is alive and in custody, and the record continues.
stops.campa: On the twelfth of June a federal appeals court denies his appeal. On the thirteenth the Bureau of Prisons closes Terminal Island altogether and disperses the men held there, and he is moved up the coast to the first of the Lompoc institutions, in the hills behind the Santa Barbara county vineyards. The customers of the exchange are being repaid at more than the face value of their claims, in dollars fixed at November 2022 prices. The register number does not change. The federal locator gives 14 December 2044.
